svg.title: Annex A7 · Review consoles on Cloudflare
svg.desc: Accounts and session, place corrections stored in D1 and read by the pipeline, and PDF upload to the data-manual branch with its refresh request.
svg.text: Annex A7 · Review consoles on Cloudflare

Two pages for authorized people, served by the same site: the places console, where each item's place is confirmed or corrected, and the documents console, where an administrator uploads the PDF no automatic route brings.
Their APIs are Cloudflare Pages Functions with a D1 database; none of this runs on GitHub Pages.
Details these boxes of the full diagram: Places console (/admin/), Documents console (/admin/documentos.html), Place reviewers, data-manual branch.
HTML and JavaScript, no build step

g.title: 1. Owner → Login and session: accounts in GEO_USERS. A user is “tester” or “admin”; without accounts the API answers 503 and explains what is missing.
2. Reviewers (tester role) → Places console: review items. Doubtful items come first.
3. Administrator (admin role) → Documents console: uploads the missing PDF. The person downloads the PDF after passing the DHN check.
4. Places console → Login and session: login.
5. Places console → Place corrections: correction. Carries the revision the person saw: if someone changed it first, it answers 409 and asks to reload.
6. Documents console → Document upload: base64 PDF + sha256.
7. Place corrections → D1 database (GEO_DB): new row + audit.
8. Login and session → D1 database (GEO_DB): session and attempts.
9. D1 database (GEO_DB) → Current corrections (public): latest revision per item.
10. Document upload → data-manual branch: blob, tree and commit. If the commit clashes with another upload (422), it is retried once on the new branch head.
11. Document upload → Request a refresh: after uploading.
12. Request a refresh → Daily update: enso-refresh. If a run is already in progress, the new one queues (production concurrency).
13. data-manual branch → Daily update: read on every run.
14. Current corrections (public) → Daily update: corrections. If the console does not answer, those of the previous publication (geo/overrides.json) are used.

Owner. Creates accounts with python -m tools.geo_users (PBKDF2-SHA256 hash, 5,000 iterations) and stores them in the GEO_USERS secret on Cloudflare: passwords are never stored. Technology: Python, wrangler.
g.text: them in the GEO_USERS secret on

g.title: Reviewers (tester role). Review doubtful items (for example, confidence below 0.8) and set, confirm or dismiss their place.
Administrator (admin role). Besides reviewing, uploads missing PDFs. The DHN asks for human verification: the person passes it in their browser and downloads the document themselves.

verification: the person passes it in

g.title: Places console. Lists the items in geo/items.json with their proposed place and confidence; each correction shows who and when. Technology: /admin/index.html, admin.js.
g.text: Lists the items in geo/items.json with their

g.title: Documents console. Shows what is missing according to data/manual-needed.json. The browser computes the sha256 and encodes the PDF in base64 before uploading it. Technology: /admin/documentos.html, documentos.js.
g.text: Shows what is missing according to
computes the sha256 and encodes the PDF in

g.title: Login and session. POST /api/geo/login checks the hash and returns a 12 h __Host- cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict). D1 keeps only the token's hash. 8 failures per user, 30 per IP in 15 min. Technology: Web Crypto, D1.
g.text: Secure, SameSite=Strict). D1 keeps only the
8 failures per user, 30 per IP in 15 min

g.title: Place corrections. Each correction is a new row with its revision: nothing is deleted or edited, and the full history and the audit log stay in D1. up to 600 per user per hour. Technology: /api/geo/corrections, D1.
g.text: Each correction is a new row with its revision:
nothing is deleted or edited, and the full
history and the audit log stay in D1.
up to 600 per user per hour

g.title: D1 database (GEO_DB). Tables for sessions, attempts, corrections, audit and uploads; shared with the alert-map A/B analytics, which has its own daily cap. Technology: Cloudflare D1, SQLite.
g.text: audit and uploads; shared with the alert-map
A/B analytics, which has its own daily cap.

g.title: Current corrections (public). GET /api/geo/overrides: each item's latest revision, without names or internal notes, cached for 60 s. Technology: /api/geo/overrides.
g.text: revision, without names or internal notes,

g.title: Document upload. POST /api/docs/upload: only DOCS_UPLOAD_ROLES (admin). Checks %PDF- and %%EOF and streams the file to GitHub without decoding it (10 ms of CPU per request). up to 25 MB and 10 uploads per hour. Technology: /api/docs/upload.
g.text: %PDF- and %%EOF and streams the file to
GitHub without decoding it (10 ms of CPU per
up to 25 MB and 10 uploads per hour

g.title: data-manual branch. Blob, tree and commit in the enso-relay/1 format (relay-manual channel): one entry per document, replaced by a new upload. Copies older than 120 days leave the index. Technology: GitHub Git Data API.
g.text: Blob, tree and commit in the enso-relay/1
document, replaced by a new upload. Copies
older than 120 days leave the index.

a.title: Annex A4: Download in GitHub Actions and per-source fallbacks

g.title: Request a refresh. After uploading, sends repository_dispatch enso-refresh so the site does not wait for the 23:37 run. Technology: repository_dispatch.
g.text: enso-refresh so the site does not wait for the

g.title: Daily update. Reads data-manual like any other collector and validates the PDF like any copy; applies the place corrections after the automatic ones: they have the last word. Technology: Python 3.12.

If something fails: what happens and which fallback takes over
After 8 failures per user or 30 per IP in 15 min it answers 429; an unknown
user takes as long as a real one.
Two reviewers correct the same item
The second gets 409 and reloads: no correction overwrites another
The console or Cloudflare does not answer
The pipeline applies the previous publication's corrections; none is lost.
The uploaded PDF is not the expected one
The pipeline recomputes the sha256 and validates the document: if it does
not match, it is not published.
The site is on GitHub Pages
The consoles need Cloudflare: /admin/ explains they are unavailable and
